newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds seen biding time ahead of U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Bunds seen biding time ahead of U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Bund futures are expected to drift on narrow ranges on Thursday, the day after setting fresh contract highs, with all eyes on U.S. jobs data this afternoon.
Traders said the morning's tone will likely be set by two events scheduled for 0900 GMT -- a speech by Bundesbank Chief Economist Otmar Issing and May industrial orders data.

The events, however, are unlikely to have a major market impact and the September DTB futures contract should drift slightly above 102.00 in the morning. At 0803 GMT, the contract was down three basis points at 102.01.

Analysts said the market will be looking for Issing to comment on remarks from French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn that France's public deficit could be "significantly higher" than the 3.0 percent forecast in the 1997 finance act.

But traders said the market is due for a bit of a breather after advancing strongly in recent sessions and especially on Wednesday when the contract broke through a tough resistance point at 102.00, hitting a high of 102.16.
The 10-year benchmark Bund was unchanged in early trade at 102.55 with the yield at 5.65 percent.
Traders said the futures contract faces technical resistance at 102.15 and support at 101.80.
They said the market is most vulnerable to strong jobs data this afternoon.
Such a report could fan worries that the U.S. economy faces wage-cost pressures and help push the Federal Reserve toward a tightening.
The spread between Bunds and Treasuries continued its narrowing trend this morning, tightening to 85 basis points from 86 basis points at the close on Wednesday.
The yield-curve likewise is continuing to flatten with the spread between two- and 10-year maturities down one basis point at 221 basis points.
